items.title: Beijing, China, China: A Pew Research Center survey showed China is viewed more positively than the United States across six continents for the first time.
items.description: A Pew Research Center survey showed China is viewed more positively than the United States across six continents for the first time.
items.rawSummary: China's economy slowed to its weakest growth since 2022 and crude oil imports hit a decade low amid the Iran conflict, even as a new Pew survey showed the country viewed more positively than the United States on six continents for the first time.
items.analysis: China's economic slowdown deepened in the second quarter, with GDP growing just 4.3% year-on-year, the slowest pace since late 2022, while crude oil imports plunged 41% in June to a ten-year low and Middle Eastern and Iranian shipments collapsed under the weight of the Iran war supply shock. In the same period, Beijing urged the U.S. and Iran to restore safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and, according to The Wall Street Journal, is preparing for a post-Putin Russia by cultivating ties with other Moscow power centers and refusing Russian gas except at below-market rates. The technological front saw continued U.S. chip exports as Nvidia H200 shipments to China began, pushing the company's shares higher, while China cemented its auto-export dominance with over 1 million vehicles shipped in June, a 73% increase. These economic and diplomatic strains coincided with a notable shift in global public opinion: a Pew Research Center survey found that China is now viewed more favorably than the United States across six continents for the first time, a soft-power development that adds a new dimension to its international positioning.

items.rawSummary: Satellite imagery shows resumed Chinese covert shipments of supplies to North Korea via border river crossings.
items.analysis: Commercial satellite imagery from Planet has revealed apparent smuggling activity at multiple sites near the Yalu River, with ‘apparent cargo’ observed at five locations between June 19–24 and another five between June 28–29, according to South Korean outlet NK Pro. The sites’ proximity to a major highway project points to likely Chinese approval of the transfers, which come against a backdrop of deepening bilateral contacts — including a June visit by CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping to Pyongyang, his first in seven years — and North Korean efforts to secure foreign currency and economic relief. The covert resupply suggests Pyongyang is leveraging both the China and Russia relationships to maximize material gain while avoiding one-sided dependency.

items.description: Former President Trump claims New York Governor Hochul terminated all data center projects, warning that investment will shift to other states and potentially benefit China.
items.rawSummary: Trump says New York Governor Hochul terminated all data center projects, pushing investment to other states.
items.analysis: Former President Trump stated that New York Governor Kathy Hochul has terminated all data center construction and future projects in the state, alleging political motives. Trump asserted that companies are now being courted by other states including Alabama, Florida, Texas, and Arizona, describing the move as a loss of jobs and tax revenue for New York. The statement, posted on social media, also claimed that data centers must pay for their own water and power with excess revenue going to state and local communities. There was no immediate response from Governor Hochul's office.

items.rawSummary: Canada to join UK-Italy-Japan fighter jet program as observer, with potential for deeper future participation.
items.analysis: Canada will become an observer in the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), gaining access to sensitive information without sharing development costs, Politico reported. The country could contribute flight simulation technology and may deepen its involvement in the sixth-generation fighter project later. The move signals Ottawa's interest in next-generation air power cooperation and could broaden the trilateral industrial base. The GCAP is a major effort by the UK, Italy, and Japan to produce an advanced combat aircraft.

items.rawSummary: President Trump prepares a primetime speech alleging Chinese interference in the 2020 election amid Republican concerns it could undercut economic messaging, while broader U.S. policy remains focused on mounting military pressure against Iran, reviving an Iraq-Syria oil pipeline, and internal political shifts over Israel aid.
items.analysis: President Trump is leaning toward expanding military operations against Iran, with the Wall Street Journal reporting options that include broader airstrikes, targeting the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility, and seizing strategic islands, while Vice President Vance reiterated the campaign aims to bring Iran to negotiations and ruled out ground troops for regime change. Vance later alleged that some within Israel’s system are running a well-funded influence campaign to prolong the war and derail U.S.-Iran talks, citing a Time magazine report. Oil prices rose above $80 per barrel amid the heightened tensions, and Washington is organizing talks to revive a dormant Iraq-Syria oil pipeline to establish a Mediterranean export route that would reduce Tehran’s strategic leverage over energy flows. In Congress, a bid to cut $3.3 billion in military aid to Israel was overwhelmingly rejected, though half of House Democrats backed the measure, signaling a notable shift within the party; the State Department approved a $1.96 billion arms sale to Saudi Arabia, and the House passed the SAVE America Act. The Pentagon also asked Congress for authority to withhold certain controlled unclassified information from FOIA disclosures on national security grounds, a move critics warn could limit public oversight of military activities. Defense Secretary Hegseth authorized a new annual testosterone deficiency screening for service members aged 30 and older, with voluntary testing for those under 30, as part of routine health assessments, a program that military medical centers like Walter Reed would help implement to sustain force readiness. President Trump is expected to allege in a primetime speech that China accessed U.S. voter data during the 2020 election and that the CIA knew but did not inform him during his first term, according to CBS News, while Politico reports that many Republicans worry the speech will revisit 2020 fraud claims, potentially distracting from economic messaging and alienating moderate voters, even as MAGA allies argue it could energize the base and boost the SAVE America Act.
